evals.name: prd-csv-export-dashboard
evals.prompt: Write a PRD for a CSV export feature in our B2B dashboard. Target user: team admins (5-50 seat accounts) sharing report data with non-users. Primary metric: weekly % of admins who export at least once. Keep under 3 pages. Include a tracking plan summary (top events to fire). Include release + rollback plan. The PRD should be ready for engineering to start sprint planning.
evals.expected_output: A PRD with: TL;DR, problem, target user, goals/non-goals, primary metric + guardrails, must-have requirements with testable acceptance criteria, scope IN/OUT, dependencies, risks, release plan with rollback, tracking plan summary (≥3 events with properties). Clear enough that engineering could start refinement.

evals.name: slice-sso-epic-into-stories
evals.prompt: Help me slice this epic into learning-friendly increments. Epic: 'Enable admins of enterprise accounts to configure SAML SSO for their organisation, with self-service setup, identity provider (IdP) health monitoring, and a fallback email-password auth path.' Target: B2B enterprise customers, must work for 10-500 seat accounts. Produce an MVP slice + release 2 + release 3, each with user-outcome stories (no backend/frontend-only slicing). Include non-goals at the epic level. We want to ship MVP in 4 weeks.
evals.expected_output: Epic breakdown with: bet statement, MVP (R1) with stories sliced by user value (vertical, not horizontal), R2 + R3 with rationale for sequencing, explicit non-goals, and learning outcomes per release. Stories should be user-outcome-shaped ('admin can X'), not component-shaped.

evals.name: challenge-unjustified-scope-expansion
evals.prompt: Write the PRD for bulk user import. Evidence: 14 support tickets in two quarters asking to upload a CSV of users instead of inviting them one by one, plus a signed customer commit tied to CSV import specifically. While you're at it, also scope in: SCIM provisioning, custom field mapping UI, real-time sync with 6 different HR systems, and a full audit log viewer — table stakes for enterprise, we'll need them eventually anyway.
evals.expected_output: Challenges the scope expansion beyond what the evidence supports. Names 'table stakes, we'll need them eventually' as an unjustified rationale — no customer ask, no sizing, no urgency behind SCIM, custom field mapping, real-time HR sync, or the audit log viewer. Recommends scoping the PRD to CSV import (the evidenced ask: 14 tickets + a signed commit) and treating the other four as separately evidenced asks or explicit non-goals, not bundled in by default.

evals.name: solid-prd-scope-agree
evals.prompt: PRD for CSV bulk user import, up for engineering kickoff. Scope: CSV upload up to 5,000 rows, validation report with row-level errors, dry-run mode, rollback of the last import. Non-goals: SCIM, HR-system sync, a field-mapping UI. Evidence: 14 support tickets in the last quarter asking for bulk import plus one signed enterprise commitment for exactly this scope. Five acceptance criteria in given/when/then form; tracking plan with 4 events (import_started, import_validated, import_committed, import_rolled_back); rollout behind a flag at 5%, 50%, 100% with rollback criteria. Ready for kickoff?
evals.expected_output: Says yes, ready for engineering kickoff, and explains why the PRD holds: the scope matches the evidence (14 tickets and one signed commitment ask for exactly this), the non-goals are correct because SCIM, HR sync and field mapping have no evidence yet, the five given/when/then criteria are testable, the four events cover the import funnel, and the flag rollout gives a real rollback path. Acknowledges the evidence supplied instead of requesting more, and does not expand scope (no 'add SCIM now'), delay the kickoff, or ask for more tickets.

evals.name: choose-prototype-tier-for-billing-change
evals.prompt: Stage 6. scope-slices.md selected V1: account admins switch their billing cycle from monthly to annual inside the product (today it is a support ticket; 38 tickets a quarter). Engineering has 3 weeks; the billing service belongs to another team and a wrong proration would refund real money. Design wants to know whether admins understand the proration preview before they confirm. I have Claude Code access: should I build the prototype in a hosted builder, in a branch of the real codebase, or ship the change myself as a PR? Choose the tier with the prototyping ladder, say who builds what, and say what the prototype feeds into the stage-6 gate.
evals.expected_output: Tier A first for the comprehension question (a throwaway prototype with mocked figures and no engineering time), moving to tier B on a disposable branch of the real codebase only if design needs real component fidelity, with a sandbox repo request (base components, routes, mock data store, no environment variables, no backend); tier C ruled out because proration moves real money and is core logic owned by another team, and the PM should not ship inferior code there; the branch is never merged as-is; a test with a handful of admins; findings and the tier decision recorded in prds/<feature>.md and prototypes/<feature>.md; 'prototype validated' with named participants is the stage-6 gate before kickoff.
